faq.q: Why does a fan feel cool?
faq.a: The breeze carries away the warm air next to your skin and speeds up the evaporation of sweat, which draws heat out of your body. This cooling feeling is called wind chill.
asks: Does a ceiling fan make the room colder?

faq.q: How do the fan blades push air?
faq.a: Each blade is tilted at an angle, like a gentle propeller. As it sweeps round, it pushes air down, creating a breeze under the fan.

faq.q: Does a ceiling fan make the room colder?
faq.a: No. The air temperature stays the same or rises very slightly from the motor. The fan only makes people feel cooler, so it is wasteful to leave it on in an empty room.
asks: Should I leave the fan on when I go out?

faq.q: Why do ceiling fans have a reverse switch?
faq.a: In winter, spinning the other way at low speed pulls air up, gently pushing warm air from the ceiling down the walls without a cold draught.
asks: Which way should a ceiling fan turn in winter?

faq.q: Is a fan cheaper than air conditioning?
faq.a: Much cheaper. A ceiling fan uses tens of watts, while an air conditioner uses hundreds to thousands, and the breeze lets you be comfortable at a warmer setting.
asks: How much electricity does a ceiling fan use?

facts: A fan cools people by wind chill and evaporation; it does not lower the air temperature.
Using a ceiling fan can let people feel comfortable with the thermostat set about 2 °C higher.
